turns.t: Mr Calder? I'm Heather, the nurse. I'll put your drops in for the eye test in a moment, but first, a couple of questions for the doctor's record. ~
Certainly. I'd rather like to get the details right, so do ask. ~
Good morning, Mr Calder. I understand light has become uncomfortable since you were ill.
Yes. Three weeks ago I had a viral illness, a fever, aches, a streaming cold. Since then, bright light, sunlight, even the strip lights in the supermarket, hurts my eyes. I squint, and my eyes water.
Is it both eyes?
Both, equally. There's no redness, and no pain as such, only a discomfort in bright light, like a glare.
Any change in your vision? ~
None whatsoever. ~
Any allergies, Mr Calder? We need it for the drops.
Well, that's an interesting one. I think I may have had a reaction to some eye drops years ago, but I can't tell you which drops, or what the reaction was. I've never been sure.
I'll note that as a possible reaction, not confirmed, substance and reaction unknown. Any medicines you take?
Just one, lansoprazole, 15 mg, once a day.
Any family history of eye problems?
My mother had glaucoma, and my uncle had macular degeneration.
Doctor, since the allergy is uncertain, shall I use the plain dilating drops without the preservative, as we normally do? ~
Please do, Heather, and watch him for ten minutes. ~
Of course.
Now, with the drops in, I'll examine you in a while. ~
Fine. ~
His eyes have dilated nicely, doctor, and there's no reaction. ~
Thank you. Mr Calder, chin on the rest, look straight ahead.
The front of both eyes is clear, with no inflammation, no redness, the pressure's normal, and the back of the eye looks healthy. ~
Is that good? ~
It is. Light sensitivity after a viral illness, with a normal examination, is common, and it usually settles over a few weeks. I'd say this is post-viral light sensitivity.
How long will it last? ~
Weeks, occasionally a couple of months. ~
Is there anything I should do? ~
Wear good sunglasses outdoors, and a brimmed hat, and don't stay in a dark room, as that can make the eyes more sensitive.
I'd been staying in rather a dim room. ~
Gradual exposure to normal light is better. ~
Understood. ~
If your vision changes, you get eye pain, redness, or a severe headache, or it's still bothering you in six weeks, come back to see me.
I will. Thank you, both. ~
